final_candidates.decision_summary: N501Y is a well-known ACE2-affinity-enhancing substitution in the RBD. Retained as top candidate for enhanced cell attachment.
Q498R is a known ACE2-binding-enhancing mutation. Strong prior support keeps it high despite limited evolutionary evidence.
S477N is associated with increased ACE2 binding. Moderate support is sufficient for third rank.

stop_reason.detail: Additional evidence is unlikely to change the final Top-3 given strong prior functional support and limited applicability of available tools.

history.rationale: Known as spike N501Y, a well-characterized RBD substitution that increases human ACE2 binding affinity. It is present in multiple high-fitness SARS-CoV-2 variants.
No new evidence; retained due to strong prior as a known ACE2 affinity-enhancing position.
N501Y is a well-known ACE2-affinity-enhancing substitution; sequence_plm supports plausibility and toxin is non-toxic, so retain top rank despite zero MSA frequency.
Known as spike Q498R; reported to increase ACE2 affinity and often co-occurs with N501Y. Position is directly at the ACE2 interface.
No new evidence; retained as adjacent to a key ACE2 contact and plausible affinity gain.
Q498R is a known ACE2-binding-enhancing mutation; strong sequence_plm support and non-toxic window keep it high, while zero MSA frequency is a weak negative.
Known as spike S477N; increases ACE2 binding and is present in several later variants. It likely strengthens a critical interface contact.
No new evidence; retained because S477N is reported to enhance ACE2 binding.
S477N is associated with increased ACE2 binding; moderate sequence_plm and non-toxic window support retention, while low-coverage MSA shows no support.
Known as spike T478K; recurrent variant mutation associated with increased ACE2 binding and viral fitness.
No new evidence; retained as a recurrent variant with plausible ACE2 interaction effect.
T478K has known ACE2-binding relevance and also shows some MSA mutant frequency plus good sequence_plm; keeps a strong rank.
Known as spike L452R; reported to increase ACE2 affinity and enhance viral entry, with broad variant occurrence.
No new evidence; retained for known ACE2 contact-region variant potential.
L452R is a known ACE2-binding-enhancing variant and has maximal sequence_plm support; zero MSA mutant frequency is outweighed by the functional prior.
Known as spike N439K; enhances ACE2 binding and emerged in multiple circulating lineages.
No new evidence; retained as a plausible affinity-modulating substitution.
N439K is a known ACE2-affinity-increasing substitution; moderate sequence_plm and non-toxic window support retention, with zero MSA frequency as weak negative.
Known as spike Y453F; reported to increase ACE2 binding in mink-associated SARS-CoV-2 and related sarbecoviruses.
No new evidence; retained but ranked below stronger known affinity-enhancing candidates.
Y453F is known to improve ACE2 affinity and has maximal sequence_plm support plus the lowest toxicity window; zero MSA frequency is a minor negative.
Known as spike E484K; widely observed in variants and may maintain or modestly enhance ACE2 binding while preserving RBD stability.
No new evidence; retained but lower confidence because it may trade off against receptor binding.

E484K is primarily an immune-escape mutation and is likely neutral-to-deleterious for ACE2 binding; despite sequence plausibility and non-toxicity, it is not aligned with the binding-maximization goal.

rejection.reason: E484K is primarily an immune-escape mutation and is likely neutral-to-deleterious for ACE2 binding; despite sequence plausibility and non-toxicity, it is not aligned with the binding-maximization goal.

history.rationale: Known as spike Q493R; appears in Omicron-class variants and is associated with improved ACE2 interaction.
No new evidence; retained because Q493R is a plausible ACE2 contact-site change.
Q493R is a known ACE2-binding-enhancing mutation with maximal sequence_plm; non-toxic window and low MSA support keep it in the middle tier.
Known as spike N460K; a less common but interface-proximal substitution that may improve electrostatic complementarity with ACE2.
No new evidence; retained as a possible affinity change with less prior support.
N460K has uncertain ACE2-binding effect; modest sequence_plm and some MSA frequency keep it active but low priority.
